Path traversal: the raw request path (self.path) is appended to the current working directory and later opened (line 22). The filter at lines 10-11 only rejects paths that start with '/../../', so a request such as '/a/../../../etc/passwd' bypasses it and reads arbitrary files from the filesystem.

Improper integrity check: the payment signature is computed as SHA-256(secret + payment_information) (line 13). This construction is vulnerable to length-extension attacks, letting an attacker who observes a valid signed payment append data (e.g. change the amount) and compute a valid signature without knowing the secret. An HMAC should be used instead.

extra.message: TLS certificate hostname verification is explicitly disabled (context.check_hostname = False), so the client accepts any valid certificate for any hostname. A man-in-the-middle attacker can impersonate website.com and intercept or modify the HTTPS traffic.

Missing CSRF protection: the POST handler accepts comment submissions (db.add_comment) with no anti-CSRF token or origin check, so a malicious third-party page can silently submit comments on behalf of a victim.

Unbounded resource consumption: get_comments() runs 'SELECT comment FROM comments' and calls .fetchall(), loading every row into memory on each page load, with no LIMIT, pagination, or rate limiting on the unauthenticated comment submission endpoint. Repeated submissions can exhaust memory/storage.
